issues.cell: *Beneath*, *A held building in an arch vault* × the bent-group sentence; W2·C2, W2·C8, W10·C2's new stretch (the bent group); attack 4; E-S4; E-V4-4.
issues.claim: Two outcomes, and a held building reshaped. (1) *Beneath*: "for the bent group it is no lawful crossing; a trace that can then cross the deck nowhere takes its own ladder (...), and by hand the stroke is refused by §7.1's lock row (`refuse.locked`, the building the blocking entity)" (adj l. 373–376). The bent-group sentence defines a lawful crossing "never in a `vault` span whose chamber seats a held building" (adj l. 405–406) and replaces "(i) an unlawful crossing by the nearest lawful one along the deck" — a bend, a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line (adj l. 408–420). Attack 4 (adj l. 556), E-S4 (adj l. 873–874: "a hand `drawWall` across that span refused `refuse.locked` naming the building") and E-V4-4 (adj l. 1115–1116) assert a refusal for the same stroke. One builder bends (the sentence), another refuses (the tests). (2) The pull keeps the span's strip "widened each side by the wall strips' widths" clear (adj l. 370–373), because a wall strip meeting a span's strip makes it "a `vault` span under the wall" with "no arch vault in it" (adj l. 358–362). The bent group excludes only the span itself: a stretch moved by (i) to the neighbouring span — clear width 6–12 m at V11 §3.24.2's masonry pitch 8–15 m and `pierWidthShare` 0.2 — lays its inner setback (6–10 m) or outer setback and glacis (10–20 m; base l. 7695–7699) across the held building's span strip, which is then read `open`: its chamber not laid, the held building standing in no chamber, or its footprint in a setback against §5.3's "footprints ∩ (wall band ⊕ setback) = ∅" (base l. 9290). J144's reading: buildings "stay held as before"; the lock sentence (adj l. 299–301).
issues.required_change: * The lawful crossing (adj l. 405–406): "and never in a `vault` span whose chamber seats a held building" → "and never where the wall's band or wall strips would meet the under-deck strip of a `vault` span whose chamber seats a held building (that strip widened each side by the wall strips' widths, *beneath*)". * *Beneath* (adj l. 373–376): "for the bent group it is no lawful crossing; a trace that can then cross the deck nowhere takes its own ladder (F-WALL at generation and at a regeneration, `walls.waited` at an epoch), and by hand the stroke is refused by §7.1's lock row (`refuse.locked`, the building the blocking entity)" → "for the bent group no lawful crossing lies in that widened strip, a crossing there moved by (i) to the nearest lawful one beyond it (by hand a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line); a trace that can then cross the deck nowhere takes its own ladder (F-WALL at generation and at a regeneration, `walls.waited` at an epoch), and by hand such a stroke, and only such, is refused by §7.1's lock row (`refuse.locked`, the building the blocking entity)". * Attack 4 (adj l. 556): "by hand `refuse.locked` naming the building (T110-2 (4))" → "by hand moved to cross under the nearest span clear of the widened strip, a fate; with none, `refuse.locked` naming the building (T110-2 (4))". * E-S4 (adj l. 873–874) and E-V4-4 (adj l. 1115–1116): "and a hand `drawWall` across that span refused `refuse.locked` naming the building" → "and a hand `drawWall` across that span moved to cross under the nearest span whose crossing keeps its band and wall strips off the widened strip, a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line, the building, its chamber and its door unchanged, and on a one-span way the same stroke refused `refuse.locked` naming the building".

issues.cell: Generation order: S3 (5)'s priced decks × S3 (8)'s weld vertices and S3 (9)'s stage-1 trace; W1·C1 at G; R7-03 (a); the fixed-place sentence; *beneath*'s pulled list; E-P4; E-S3.
issues.claim: In the base S3 "the gate routes are solved first, the stage-1 boundary is the travel-cost level set over them, the gates are where the routes cross it, and the castle weld and the moat are placed on the trace pulled from that boundary ... before S4 commits a single way" (base l. 5450–5454): (5) "Gate routes, solved (not committed) ... with S4's cost function ... S4 commits exactly these routes" (base l. 5535–5538); (8) sites the castle and its weld vertices (base l. 5579); (9) "the registered `EnceinteStrategy` traces the enceinte here by S5a's rules", anchors, water and the 40 m pull included (base l. 5591–5600); S4 "commits the gate routes solved at S3 ... without re-solving" (base l. 5755); §2.7 (6) places a raised way's stations "at generation inside S4's ... route solve" (base l. 2557–2560). So a gate route's deck is solved before the stage-1 trace and the weld, and committed after them, unchanged. The rulings fix no order. R7-03 (a) re-solves a gate route only where its first point at `T = t_1` lies on a deck, excluding "every deck edge whose two ends lie on either side of the stage-1 boundary" (adj l. 623–627) — the trace, pulled up to 40 m (or `wall.barrierReachM`) off that boundary at S3 (9), may still cross the deck or lay its band over its ramp or foot. *Beneath*'s pull reads "a standing raised way" (adj l. 344–347), and E-P4 adds S3 (8)'s weld filter only for "(a held one at a regeneration ...)" (adj l. 976–977): so at a first generation S3 (8)–(9) read no deck. S4 then commits the deck unchanged, while the fixed-place sentence makes "A raised way created after the wall" keep the trace's fixed places outside its zone (adj l. 441–444) — which a route S4 never re-solves cannot do; E-S3 nevertheless asserts "the viaduct, laid after the stage-1 trace, keeping that anchor outside its fixed-place zone" (adj l. 847–849). Builders differ: S3 (8)–(9) give way to (5)'s decks (anchor and water gate moved, weld filtered, ramps impassable); or the deck stands across the trace, or with a fixed place in its zone, failing T110-2 (2)'s "0 road decks across a trace standing when laid" or the "0 ... in a fixed-place zone" bar; or S4 re-solves (against "without re-solving").
issues.required_change: * R7-03 (a), after "a route the re-solve cannot serve takes F-ROUTE's ladder (§5.2), reported." (adj l. 628–629) add: "The raised stretches of (5)'s routes, so re-solved, are standing raised ways for every later step of S3, laid before the stage-1 trace: S3 (8)'s weld filter and S3 (9)'s pull, anchors and water gates read their courses, their ramps, stairs and feet, their under-deck strips and fixed-place zones as *beneath* and the fixed-place sentence read a standing raised way's (the pull keeping an arterial's crossing as §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2) keeps it), and S4 commits them unchanged; a raised way S4 solves after S3 (a route of its own) is created after the trace and keeps clear of it." * *Beneath*'s pulled list (adj l. 344–345): "S3's and S5a's at generation and at a regeneration" → "S3's (reading (5)'s re-solved decks as standing, §4.2 S3 (7)) and S5a's at generation and at a regeneration". * E-P4 (adj l. 976–977): "(a held one at a regeneration; §2.7's crossing table, the fixed-place sentence)" → "(the raised stretches of (5)'s routes at generation, a held one at a regeneration too; §2.7's crossing table, the fixed-place sentence)". * E-S3 (adj l. 847–849): "a spur town whose gorge-side stretch anchors on the rim where S4's priced viaduct would cross the gorge — the viaduct, laid after the stage-1 trace, keeping that anchor outside its fixed-place zone —" → "a spur town whose gorge-side stretch would anchor on the rim where a gate route's priced viaduct crosses the gorge — the anchor, laid after that viaduct (S3 (9) after (5)), moved along the rim clear of its fixed-place zone with its tower — and, on a second run, where a viaduct on an S4 route of its own would cross there, that viaduct, laid after the trace, keeping the anchor outside its fixed-place zone —".

issues.cell: C8 for every row whose event acts on the wall itself — W2·C8 (a moved trace vertex, a re-anchored stretch, a carve's re-trace), W4·C8, W7·C8, W8·C8, W10·C8, W11·C8, W13·C8; C13 on a declared raised way; E-S4's fixtures; §7.1's declaration row.
issues.claim: C8 reads "held — the raised way, the wall or both locked, pinned or declared (a drawn wall locked by its drawing, §7.2) — as the same cell unheld ...; an op that targets a held thing itself — a `convert`, `delete`, `repairWall` or `placeGate` on a locked wall, an edit of a locked raised way — is §7.1's lock row's, no meeting" (adj l. 458–461). §7.2: "a drawn feature is locked besides", drawn walls "locked by default", and "Its author changes it by a new declaration (a handle drag, §7.1)" (base l. 10812–10820); §7.1's first row refuses a map event that "crosses, targets or moves a locked or pinned entity" (base l. 10631); §4.11 *Other crossings* returns a carve re-tracing a locked run as an F-EDIT conflict. The C8 cells of the rows whose event is an op on the wall read "as Wn·C2, no `refuse.locked`" with no word for which side is held (W2 adj l. 494, W4 l. 496, W7 l. 499, W13 l. 505; W8, W10, W11 "as Wn·C2"). On a drawn wall — the common hand case — one builder runs the cell (bend, no refusal: the author's handle drag), another refuses (`refuse.locked`: the column's targeted op; F-EDIT for a carve's re-trace). The same split reaches C13: a declared raised way is drawn, so locked by its drawing, and "an edit of a locked raised way — is §7.1's lock row's"; yet E-S4 runs "a standing declared viaduct's course re-shaped so that a stretch of it crosses the ring — ... no `refuse.locked`" (adj l. 877–880), T110-2 (4) changes "the viaduct's Arch spacing" on "a declared one-span masonry viaduct" (base l. 18570, 18582), and E-S4's hand rows act on "the run beneath" (adj l. 860) — the hand `drawWall`'s run (locked by its drawing) or the epoch circuit's, unsaid. A build that refuses fails E-S4; one that runs the cell contradicts C8's own description. And §7.1's "a declaration contradicting a dossier fact or a lock (item 101) | refused | ... | `refuse.dossierOwned`, `refuse.locked`" row (base l. 10636) keeps no exemption (E-D1 rewrites only the first row's parenthesis, adj l. 1003–1010), so VDC6-01's own case — a T4 aqueduct declared across a drawn wall — can still be read as refused there.
issues.required_change: * C8 (adj l. 458–461): "an op that targets a held thing itself — a `convert`, `delete`, `repairWall` or `placeGate` on a locked wall, an edit of a locked raised way — is §7.1's lock row's, no meeting" → "an op that targets a held thing itself — a `convert`, `delete`, `repairWall`, `placeGate`, moved vertex or re-anchor on a wall, or an edit of a raised way, that the user locked or pinned (T10 `hold`) — is §7.1's lock row's, no meeting (a carve re-tracing such a run, §4.11 *Other crossings*' conflict); a drawn wall or a declared raised way changed by its author's new declaration (§7.2 *Declared means held*: a handle drag, a re-shape, a stepper, a `convert`, `delete`, `repairWall` or `placeGate`) is no such op and takes its cell". * Each C8 cell of W2, W4, W7, W8, W10, W11 and W13: "as Wn·C2[, no `refuse.locked`]" → "as Wn·C2, no `refuse.locked` (the raised way held, or a drawn wall changed by its author); a wall the user locked or pinned: §7.1's lock row, no meeting". * E-S4 (adj l. 859–860): "a hand `convert` `breach` and `dismantle` of the run beneath (W4)" → "a hand `convert` `breach` and `dismantle` of the epoch circuit's run beneath (W4)", and at the clause's end add "; each hand row run again on the hand `drawWall`'s run (drawn, so changed by its author: the cell's outcome) and on a run the user locked (§7.1's lock row: `refuse.locked`, nothing written)". * E-D1, a second change: §7.1's row "| a declaration contradicting a dossier fact or a lock (item 101) |" → "| a declaration contradicting a dossier fact or a lock (item 101; never a meeting of a wall and a raised way, §2.7's crossing table, its lock sentence) |". (The amend seat may rule instead that a drawn feature's lock refuses its author's edits too; then E-S4's declared viaduct, T110-2 (4)'s re-spacing and the hand rows on the drawn run are run unlocked, and the cells say so.)

issues.cell: W12·C8 (V05's landfall over a held run or beneath a held raised way).
issues.claim: W12·C8 reads "as W12·C2 · T-V5-14" (adj l. 504), and W12·C2 gives "the run `breached` by the landfall's wall row, the spans and supports its footprint covers `ruined` by theirs". V05 §3.16 (2) takes the covered set "less every locked or pinned entity and the plots that hold one (kept content, as §3.3's fixed obstacles; the ruin laps around them)" (V05 l. 1317–1319; F-SKY-LANDFALL, V05 l. 1383), and T-V5-14 asserts it on this very row: "With the aqueduct locked, it is kept as content the ruin laps around (V05 §3.16 (2); F-SKY-LANDFALL), `members` holding none of its parts, and the run beneath is `breached` all the same" (V05 l. 2570–2572), with "a locked wall kept". A declared raised way or wall is pinned by its declaring event (§7.2). The landfall is no meeting of two similar structures, so J144 and the lock sentence ("No meeting of two similar structures is refused, skipped or altered for a lock", adj l. 287–288) do not reach it, yet the cell gives the held side C2's outcome. Two units, two outcomes for one case (R7-01's grading).
issues.required_change: W12·C8: "as W12·C2 · T-V5-14" → "the held side kept, never covered — content the ruin laps around (V05 §3.16 (2); F-SKY-LANDFALL), no member — the other side as W12·C2 (a held raised way's spans and supports kept and the run beneath `breached`; a held run kept and the spans over it `ruined`) · T-V5-14". The lock sentence, after "the lock axis is one case (column C8)." (adj l. 288): add "A hazard or an engine op that is no meeting of two similar structures — a landfall (row W12), the decay (W5), an epoch's conversion of a held wall (V06 §3.1) — keeps every lock and pin as §7.2, V05 §3.16 (2) and V06 §3.1 keep them; the lock sentence reaches only the changes a meeting makes."

issues.cell: The set's lock bars (blind spot (c)): V06's T-V6-4 and its *history × locks* row; §15.2's O9 (b); §13.2's T101-5.
issues.claim: T-V6-4: "a locked or pinned entity, a declared place (item 101 R13) ... are never struck, converted, closed or moved by the engine ... 0 violations" (V06 l. 4127); V06's edge row "the history × locks | a locked or pinned entity is never struck, converted or moved (V06 §3.1)" (V06 l. 3323); §15.2's O9 (b) "locked preserved 100 %" [C] (base l. 20336); T101-5 "no declaration contradicts a dossier fact or a lock without a refusal carrying its reason and at least one closest alternative" (base l. 18441). Under the lock sentence an epoch circuit removes a locked arch vault's chamber and a held raised way's chambers (W1·C8; E-S4, adj l. 869–872), a regeneration leaves a locked chamber unlaid (W3·C8), and by hand a `drawWall` changes a locked vault and a raised road makes a gate in a drawn wall with no refusal (the fate *reshaped*). No END conforms these bars (Part H's sweeps name §7.2, §5.3, §7.4 and V06 §3.1 only: E-D8 – E-D10, E-V6-12). A correct build fails T-V6-4's 0-violation count and O9 (b)'s CI check; a build tuned to pass them keeps the locked chamber, against W1·C8 – W3·C8. Two builds.
issues.required_change: New END lines. * Under V06 (E-V6-14): T-V6-4 "are never struck, converted, closed or moved by the engine" → "are never struck, converted, closed or moved by the engine — but a wall, a raised way or an arch vault, held in its placement and changed in shape where they meet by §2.7's crossing table (its lock sentence), each change a `reshaped` entry —"; and the *history × locks* row "a locked or pinned entity is never struck, converted or moved (V06 §3.1)" → "... (V06 §3.1; a wall, a raised way or an arch vault in its placement only, §2.7's crossing table, the lock sentence)". * Under scope (E-S11): §15.2's O9 (b) "locked preserved 100 %" → "locked preserved 100 % (a wall, a raised way or an arch vault in its placement, its shape where they meet §2.7's crossing table's, the lock sentence)"; T101-5 "no declaration contradicts a dossier fact or a lock without a refusal" → "no declaration contradicts a dossier fact or a lock without a refusal (a meeting of a wall and a raised way contradicts no lock: §2.7's crossing table, the lock sentence)".

issues.cell: *Down before the wall*: the gate made in a held wall — W1·C1 (G, R, E), the C1 "—" cells of W2 and W3, C13's re-shaped road deck; the lock sentence's list; E-D1; §5.3's gate rows; §4.8 *Gates*.
issues.claim: The lock sentence lists "a gate made where a road deck's carried way crosses a wall" among the meeting's changes (adj l. 284–285); *down before the wall* makes it on every path — "its route crossing the trace on ground part 0 through the gate there ... — a gate made there in a held wall too, its `reshaped` entry (the lock sentence) —" (adj l. 328–331), and by hand "its ground way making its gate there — in a held wall the fate *reshaped* (G2)" (adj l. 335); veto 10 (adj l. 239–241). Unruled: (1) at an epoch "an epoch's growth crosses at gates alone" (§5.3, base l. 9287), so an epoch route's priced deck brought down before an inner held ring finds "the gate there" only where one stands — one builder makes a new gate in the held ring (the cell), another routes to a standing gate (§5.3); (2) at a regeneration a held ring is a fixed input (§7.2 *Protection*) whose gates are its own: a gate made in it passes §4.8's "exactly N, by construction" (base l. 7729) and F-WALL's "main gates = N exactly" (base l. 9203) or re-counts N — unstated — and no op is named that makes a gate in a standing held ring at S4 (S3's gates are made on the boundary it derives; §7.3's S7 operator is a hand operator); (3) by hand the carried way is a ground way, and E-D1's exemption names only "a meeting of two similar structures — a wall and a raised way" (adj l. 1006), so "a drawn way across a locked entity" still reads as refusing the ground way's crossing of a drawn wall. Only the hand case is tested (E-S2, adj l. 838–840).
issues.required_change: * *Down before the wall* (adj l. 330–331): "— a gate made there in a held wall too, its `reshaped` entry (the lock sentence) —" → "— at generation, at a regeneration and at an epoch through a gate already standing there (a held wall's gates are its own: the route is solved to one of them, its deck coming down before it, else the solver's ladder or not built, reported), so no gate is made in a held wall but by hand —". * By hand (adj l. 335): "its ground way making its gate there — in a held wall the fate *reshaped* (G2) —" → "its ground way making its gate there by §7.3's S7 operator, a gate on ground part 0 counted as any drawn way's (§5.3's gate row) — in a held wall the fate *reshaped* (G2), §7.1's lock row not refusing it —". * The lock sentence (adj l. 284–285): "a gate made where a road deck's carried way crosses a wall" → "a gate made by hand where a road deck's carried way crosses a wall". * E-D1 adds to its parenthesis: "nor a raised road's ground way making its gate in a locked or pinned wall it comes down before (§2.7's crossing table, *down before the wall*),". * E-S2 adds: "; a regeneration (keep) of a CITY whose stage-1 ring was drawn by hand, an S4 route priced on a deck across it — the deck down before the ring, the route through one of the ring's standing gates, no gate made, the ring's gate count unchanged". (If the program wants a gate made at generation and at an epoch instead, the ruling must name the op, N's re-count and §5.3's epoch row in the same words.)

issues.cell: No row: a standing wall re-sectioned on its kept trace.
issues.claim: Three events change a standing wall's band and strips on an unchanged trace. V07 §3.11's palisade REPLACEMENT: "the wall is rebuilt on the palisade's trace — `setAttr` of the enceinte's kind to `inner`, `material: 'stone'`, its full stretches taking the stone section and its light ones the parapet" (V07 l. 2288–2291), at an epoch. A hand `setAttr` of "a stretch's grade, `profile/<arc ordinal>/grade` = `full` · `light` · `closure` ...: an edited path S7's operator keeps as a fixed input" (base l. 10588). "Re-derive from S7 when the enceinte kind changes" (§7.3's S7 row, base l. 10927). §4.8: "the wall's thickness, height, walk and tower spacing read its class's row" (base l. 7716–7718). No row W1–W13 is such an event (W3 re-lays a ring by W1's rules but keeps no trace; W10 repairs a run's condition). A palisade crossing a declared aqueduct under a span, its narrow band at most meeting a support's edge (the lawful crossing, adj l. 403–404), rebuilt in stone on the same line: its band's half now covers the support past its edge (against *Where the line crosses*, adj l. 339–342, and item 110 (b)'s arch as the program reads it); its wider strips may newly meet another `vault` span's strip (a held building's among them, PRB7-01); a light stretch re-graded `full` takes towers at a spacing, one inside the strip. Builders: the band through the pier; the stretch re-traced by the bent group; the old section kept there; a refusal.
issues.required_change: Block 1's table gains a row after W13 (and the table's "13 rows" become 14 wherever counted): "| **W14** a standing wall re-sectioned on its kept trace — V07 §3.11's palisade REPLACEMENT rebuilt on the palisade's trace (E), a hand `setAttr` of a stretch's grade or of the enceinte's kind, re-derived from S7 (H; §7.3's S7 row) | — | the new section by *beneath*: where its band's half would meet an aqueduct's standing support past its edge or a ramp, stair or foot, or its band or strips a held building's widened vault strip, the run there re-traced by the bent-group sentence (a re-traced run, as a carve's), else (G3); a `vault` span the new band or strips meet read `open` (its chamber removed; a held one's the fate *reshaped* or a `reshaped` entry), one they no longer meet laid again; a tower or gate the new section's law places in the under-deck strip moved along (*No gate and no tower*) · T110-2 (4)·S (H), T-V7-48 (E) | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | no meeting · — | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | as W14·C2 (the REPLACEMENT at a village rung) · T-V7-48 | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | — | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | as W14·C2 · T110-2 (4)·S | §7.3's S7 operator over the run (strips re-cut, S10's step (0)); V07's REPLACEMENT batch · gates kept on ground part 0 · by hand `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line, each move a fate |". ENDs: scope's E-S4 adds "; a light stretch of the hand `drawWall` above re-graded `full` under the standing aqueduct — its wider band kept to a lawful crossing by the bent-group sentence, a fate (row W14)"; V07's E-V7-1 adds "; a palisade under the declared aqueduct rebuilt in stone on its trace by the REPLACEMENT — its band at most meeting a support's edge, re-traced locally where it would not (row W14)".

issues.cell: *Beneath*'s rules for pulled traces (W1 at G and E, W3) and the bent group's (ii)–(iii); *where the line crosses*; *the cap*.
issues.claim: The rules test the line, the bars the band. A pulled trace "treats a standing raised way's ramps, stairs and feet and an aqueduct's standing supports as impassable" (adj l. 344–347) — its line; S10 then lays the band at its half-widths by §4.8's rows (wall thickness 2–3 m, base l. 7695), and "The band is laid through every support standing in it — a road deck's, or the edge of an aqueduct's that its band's half meets" (adj l. 351–353) — with no measure of "the edge". A pulled line passing 1 m off an aqueduct's ring lays a band whose half covers 1–2 m of that pier (at `pierMinCm` 150, the whole pier): the aqueduct then crosses the wall at a pier, against *Where the line crosses* (adj l. 339–342) and behaviour change 8. A pulled line passing 1 m beside a ramp lays its band over the ramp, against T110-2 (3)'s "no ramp, stair or foot in the band or the channel" (base l. 18567). For the bent group, by contrast, a lawful crossing keeps "its band's half at most meeting a standing support's edge" (adj l. 404) — the band tested. And (ii)–(iii) move a part "by that side's edge" (adj l. 412–416): the line on the strip's edge, its band's half (2–3 m) reaching past the 1 m strip margin (V11 §3.24.2's `stripMarginM`) into the deck's plan over every pier along it, where *the cap* covers only "beneath a standing part of the deck" (adj l. 353–358) and says nothing of a band partly beneath it. Builders differ: the impassable set widened by the band's half or not; (ii)'s line at the edge or offset; a band partly beneath capped or not.
issues.required_change: * *Beneath* (adj l. 344–347): "treats a standing raised way's ramps, stairs and feet and an aqueduct's standing supports as impassable" → "treats a standing raised way's ramps, stairs and feet, each widened by the band's half there (§4.8's rows along the stretch profile), and an aqueduct's standing supports, each widened so that the band's half at most touches the ring (*the edge*), as impassable to its line". * (adj l. 352): "or the edge of an aqueduct's that its band's half meets" → "or an aqueduct's whose ring its band's half at most touches (*the edge*: the ring's boundary, the band entering no further)". * (ii) (adj l. 413–414): "by that side's edge between its entry and exit points" → "by the line along that side's edge offset outward by the band's half there, between its entry and exit points, so the band stays outside the under-deck strip"; (iii) (adj l. 415): "by the line to the nearest point of the edge" → "by the line to the nearest point of that offset line".

issues.cell: *Over the band* × the fixed-place sentence: W1·C1, W1·C11, C13's re-shaped aqueduct; the paths note; E-V6-4; E-D2; E-P1.
issues.claim: The fixed-place sentence: "A raised way created after the wall keeps every fixed place outside its own fixed-place zone", the zone being "its under-deck strip widened each side by the wall strips' widths" (adj l. 430–432, 441–444). *Over the band*: "its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers and of its fixed places" (adj l. 315–317) and "S6's aqueduct having kept its strip clear of the anchors and weld vertices the trace records" (adj l. 319–320); the paths note: "its strip clear of the towers, gates and fixed places" (adj l. 484); E-V6-4 at the founding: fixed places "impassable to the course's supports, ramps, stairs and feet and to its clearing ((7))" — the clearing is the strip (V06 l. 2837–2838) — and "its under-deck strip clear of the curtain's towers, gates and fixed places (impassable above)" (adj l. 1176–1181); E-D2: "bent clear of that wall's towers, gates and fixed places" (adj l. 1016). A fixed place 1–20 m outside the strip but inside the zone: V06's founding and the hand bend admit it, the base sentence and the bars ("0 gates, towers, anchors or weld vertices in a fixed-place zone", E-S3) forbid it. Two units, two courses.
issues.required_change: * *Over the band* (adj l. 315–317): "its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers and of its fixed places" → "its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers, and its fixed-place zone of the trace's fixed places"; (adj l. 319–320) "S6's aqueduct having kept its strip clear of the anchors and weld vertices the trace records" → "S6's aqueduct having kept its fixed-place zone clear of the anchors, water gates and weld vertices the trace records"; (adj l. 322) "or its strip clear of the gates, towers and fixed places" → "or its strip clear of the gates and towers and its fixed-place zone of the fixed places". * The paths note (adj l. 484): "its strip clear of the towers, gates and fixed places" → "its strip clear of the towers and gates and its fixed-place zone of the fixed places". * E-V6-4: "enceinte towers, gates and fixed places (§2.7's crossing table, the fixed-place sentence), ... are **impassable** to the course's supports, ramps, stairs and feet and to its clearing ((7))" → "enceinte towers and gates ... are **impassable** to the course's supports, ramps, stairs and feet and to its clearing ((7)), and each fixed place of a standing curtain to its fixed-place zone (§2.7's crossing table, the fixed-place sentence)"; and "its under-deck strip clear of the curtain's towers, gates and fixed places (impassable above)" → "its under-deck strip clear of the curtain's towers and gates and its fixed-place zone of the curtain's fixed places (impassable above)". * E-D2 (both places): "clear of that wall's towers, gates and fixed places" / "clear of its towers, gates and fixed places" → "clear of that wall's towers and gates, its fixed-place zone clear of the wall's fixed places" / "clear of its towers and gates, its fixed-place zone clear of its fixed places"; E-P1: "its under-deck strip clear of the trace's gates, towers and fixed places" → "its under-deck strip clear of the trace's gates and towers and its fixed-place zone of the trace's fixed places".

issues.cell: W13 (a slid gate, a placed gate); *No gate and no tower*; E-D3; attack 7; veto 13; E-S4; E-V9-2.
issues.claim: W13·C2: "at an `at` or a slide's end inside the under-deck strip, moved along the trace to the nearest point clear of it" (adj l. 505); E-D3: "a `placeGate` or a slid gate moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip" (adj l. 1028–1029). But attack 7: "The gate goes back along the trace" (adj l. 561–562); veto 13: "a gate the user places or slides into the strip moves back along the wall" (adj l. 248–249); E-S4: "moved back along the trace clear of it" (adj l. 862–863); E-V9-2: "moves back along the trace clear of it" (adj l. 1273). A slide ending past the strip's middle lies nearest the far edge: the base moves the gate on, the tests and V09's line move it back. For an `at` (or a slide's end) at the middle, no tie rule.
issues.required_change: W13·C2: "moved along the trace to the nearest point clear of it" → "moved along the trace clear of it — a slid gate back to the strip's edge on the side its grip left, a `placeGate`'s `at` to the nearer edge (ties: the edge nearer the trace's first vertex in vertex order) —"; *No gate and no tower* (adj l. 383–384): "and a gate the user places or slides there (`placeGate`, a gate's grip) along the trace" → "and a gate the user places or slides there (`placeGate`, a gate's grip) along the trace as row W13 says"; E-D3: "a `placeGate` or a slid gate moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip" → "a slid gate moved back along the trace, and a `placeGate` to the nearer edge, clear of the under-deck strip (row W13)".

issues.cell: The lawful crossing and *Where the line crosses* at a `cleared` support (C5): W1·C5, W2·C5, W3·C5.
issues.claim: The lawful crossing: "meeting the deck line once: under an aqueduct's span, its band's half at most meeting a standing support's edge; under a road deck's span or at its support" (adj l. 403–405); *Where the line crosses*: "It crosses an aqueduct's deck line under a span" (adj l. 341–342). But C5: "a trace laid after a support is `cleared` passes through its ring as open ground" (adj l. 452–453); W2·C5: "a `cleared` ring open ground" (adj l. 494); W3·C5: "through a `cleared` ring as open ground" (adj l. 495); T110-2 (4): "a hand `drawWall` across a raised way with a `ruined` span and a `cleared` support in its line — ... the trace through the cleared ring" (base l. 18578–18579). A line through a cleared aqueduct support's ring meets the deck line at its station, not under a span: the bent group's (i) moves it to the nearest span (a fate), C5 and the test keep it through the ring. The two sentences of *Where the line crosses* disagree there for a pulled trace too.
issues.required_change: The lawful crossing (adj l. 403–404): "under an aqueduct's span," → "under an aqueduct's span or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground: both its spans fallen and never rebuilt, C5),"; *Where the line crosses* (adj l. 341–342): "It crosses an aqueduct's deck line under a span," → "It crosses an aqueduct's deck line under a span or through a `cleared` support's ring (C5),".

issues.cell: The bent-group list × V06 §3.7.6 (1) and (5): an epoch's re-anchored stretch (W1 at E).
issues.claim: The bent group lists "a re-anchored stretch" without a path (adj l. 398–399); W1's event cell has "an epoch's circuit, contraction or re-anchored stretch (V06 §3.7)" (adj l. 493); *beneath*'s pulled list names "an epoch's circuit, contraction or dossier-admitted circuit" — no re-anchored stretch (adj l. 344–346). V06 §3.7.6: "Every rule of this section binds every trace the engine makes — a new circuit, a shorter ring, a repaired or re-anchored stretch: 1. ... The trace is the registered `EnceinteStrategy`'s" (V06 l. 1552–1555), and (5) makes the raised way's supports, ramps, stairs and feet impassable in the cost field for "a re-anchored or repaired stretch" (V06 l. 1594–1600). One builder pulls the epoch's re-anchored stretch (the cost path's span, a gate by the pin rule); another lays it and moves it by (i) (the nearest lawful span, the spine-order tie). Two units, two outcomes — VCS-r6-02's class.
issues.required_change: The bent group (adj l. 398–399): "a re-anchored stretch" → "a stretch re-anchored by hand (an epoch's re-anchored stretch is the `EnceinteStrategy`'s, V06 §3.7.6 (1), and takes the pull's rules)"; *beneath*'s pulled list (adj l. 345–346): "an epoch's circuit, contraction or dossier-admitted circuit" → "an epoch's circuit, contraction, re-anchored stretch or dossier-admitted circuit". (Or the reverse, with an END amending V06 §3.7.6 (1) and (5).)

issues.cell: *A `vault` span under the wall*: the chamber laid again — W2·C2 (a moved vertex leaving a span), W4's last dismantle of an absorbed record, W7·C2 (ways other than the ring road; the moat), W8·C2, W11·C2.
issues.claim: While a wall's band or strip lies over a `vault` span the span is "an `open` span to §4.3's crossing rule, the way-and-channel table and V01 §3.17.3 (2)–(3), the band, strips and moat laid through it" (adj l. 362–365), so S7's intervallum and quays, S5c's streets, a stage-2 seed's lanes, a village track and the moat (row e) may cross its strip; "its record unchanged ..., so it reads `vault` again, V04 laying its chamber again, once none lies there" (adj l. 365–366). V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1) lays the chamber "found by its key or created" over "the span's under-deck rectangle" with no exception (V04 l. 1695–1702). R7-04 (d) re-routes only `wallToWay`'s own ring road (adj l. 689–695); V06 keeps a ring's moat "as still water" after `wallToWay` or `absorbWall` (V06 l. 3311). So after `wallToWay`, a hand delete (W11), the last dismantle of an absorbed record (W8, W4) or a moved trace vertex leaving the span (W2), the chamber is laid at grade across a standing lane or street, or in the moat's water; T110-2's lead counts "way corridors over ... a `vault` span's strip reading ... `vault` spans no wall stands over" (E-S0, adj l. 803–807), which the build then fails. Builders: lay it over the corridor or water, withhold it, cut the way, re-route the way.
issues.required_change: *A `vault` span under the wall* (adj l. 365–366): "so it reads `vault` again, V04 laying its chamber again, once none lies there" → "so it reads `vault` again, V04 laying its chamber again, once none lies there and no way's corridor or channel laid while it read `open` crosses its under-deck strip (`wallToWay`'s ring road excepted, re-routed by row (c)); such a span stays read `open` while that corridor or water lies there, so no chamber is laid across a way or in water". R7-06 (b)'s one wording and E-S0's lead: "`vault` spans no wall stands over" → "`vault` spans no wall, and no way corridor or channel laid while they read `open`, stands over". END under V04 (E-V4-6, a third change): (1)'s "or a run of an absorbed record not yet `dismantled` crosses it" adds "or a way's corridor or a channel laid while it read `open` crosses it". E-S7 adds: "the intervallum and the moat that passed under that span while the wall stood — the span read `open` while they lie there, no chamber over the lane or in the water".

issues.cell: *No gate and no tower* and the fixed-place zone at a fallen span — W1·C3, W1·C4, W2·C3, W2·C4, W3·C3, W3·C4, C6 — then the span's repair (C10).
issues.claim: The way-and-channel lead now says "whatever a span's `state`: a `ruined` or `cleared` span's strip is crossed by this rule as a standing one's" (adj l. 517–518; R7-04 (e)); neither *No gate and no tower in the under-deck strip* (adj l. 376–385) nor the fixed-place sentence (adj l. 430–433) says whether a fallen span's strip counts, and W1·C3 says only "*beneath*, own top beneath the fallen span" (adj l. 493). A trace laid after a span fell (an epoch circuit, a hand stretch, a regeneration after a lapse) may place a gate, a tower or an anchor under the fallen span; `repairRaised` — C10, "as C2, the repair writing the raised way alone" (adj l. 462) — then stands the span over it: a gate under a deck, a tower above the soffit, against T110-2's "0 gates or towers in an under-deck strip". The sweep makes each state before the wall event only (C10 is "C3's `ruined` span repaired by `repairRaised`" first, adj l. 731), so no test lays a wall at C3 and then repairs the span.
issues.required_change: *No gate and no tower* (adj l. 376–377): "— one the wall's law would place there moves to the nearest point clear of it:" → "— the strip of every span, standing or fallen (`ruined` or `cleared`, read as the way-and-channel table reads a fallen span), and every fixed-place zone likewise, so a span `repairRaised` raises again stands over no gate, tower or fixed place; one the wall's law would place there moves to the nearest point clear of it:". E-S0's sweep, after "C10, C3's `ruined` span repaired by `repairRaised`;" add "and, in each clause whose wall event lays a trace, the C3 run once more with that span repaired after the event — no gate or tower under it;".

issues.cell: C12 × R7-04 (c): a frame growth's extension past a structural bound (W1·C12, W2·C12, and every C12 cell through *down before the wall* and *over the band*).
issues.claim: C12: "the extension keeps the deck's course ((7)), so it is no course laid: where it crosses a band its new supports are slid off that band by (3)" (adj l. 462–465); *down before the wall*: "a frame growth's extension, which keeps the deck's course, is no course laid (C12)" (adj l. 327). R7-04 (c) (adj l. 679–686): past a bound "its course bends ... to the nearest course from that station to the new ring whose clear spans and piers fit"; "with none, it keeps the straight course, each station (1)–(2) place standing where it falls — a support in a water face kept there, a pier past `maxPierM` kept". Unruled: (1) whether a bent extension is a course laid — a road deck's bent course crossing a standing trace (*down before the wall*), an aqueduct's bent strip over a standing trace's gates, towers or fixed places (*over the band*; the fixed-place sentence); (2) "the straight course" against "the deck's course" (a polyline); (3) whether "each station ... standing where it falls" also skips (3)'s slide off a band, a way's corridor and a square, or only the bound's water and height. Two builders, three places.
issues.required_change: R7-04 (c)'s text: "to the nearest course from that station to the new ring whose clear spans and piers fit," → "to the nearest course from that station to the new ring whose clear spans and piers fit and which meets each standing wall as C13's re-shaped stretch does (an aqueduct *over the band*, a road deck never across a standing trace, its strip clear of gates and towers and its fixed-place zone of fixed places),"; "with none, it keeps the straight course, each station (1)–(2) place standing where it falls —" → "with none, it keeps the deck's course, each station (1)–(2) place slid by (3) off every obstacle but water and omitted nowhere —". C12 (adj l. 465) adds: "; past a bound the extension bends by (7), the bent course meeting a standing wall as C13's re-shape does".

issues.cell: (G3)'s ladders off the hand path: F-WALL at generation and at a regeneration, `walls.waited` at an epoch, VS3's ladder at a village; the held building's, the bent group's and the fixed-place sentence's citations of them.
issues.claim: (G3) sends the newer trace to "F-WALL's ladder (§5.2)" at generation and at a regeneration, "`walls.waited`" at an epoch and "VS3 ... its own ladder (V07 §3.13)" at a village (adj l. 296–299); *A held building* (adj l. 373–374), the bent group (adj l. 421–425) and the fixed-place sentence (adj l. 439–441) cite them. F-WALL's detection (a self-intersecting or unclosed trace, an unanchored end, fewer crossings than N, a non-gate way) and rungs (re-offset, union-simplify, anchor by attraction, divert arterials, posterns, cut a way) name no raised-way meeting (base l. 9203); V07 §3.13's ladders (F-V-PAL, F-V-ANCHOR, F-V-GATE ...; V07 l. 2743–2746) have none; V06 §2.10's `walls.waited` reads "none waits for a raised way" and `raised.waited` lists no course waiting for a strip or zone it cannot clear (V06 l. 755, 770). No END writes any of them, and no clause runs (G3) at generation, a regeneration, an epoch or a village (E-S1 runs only a hand aqueduct). A builder at S3 or S5a may re-offset (and pass through a support), leave the stage unwalled, or ignore the meeting.
issues.required_change: New END lines. * Under pipeline (E-P9): §5.2's F-WALL row, detection adds "; a trace with no lawful crossing of a standing raised way, a fixed place with no clear point in reach, or a held building's widened vault strip it cannot keep clear (§2.7's crossing table, (G3))", and its ladder, before the last rung, adds "→ for a raised-way meeting: the boundary re-pulled once with that raised way's fixed-place zone impassable but at its lawful crossings → that stage left unwalled, reported (`W_RAISED_MEETING`)". * Under V06 (E-V6-15): §2.10's `walls.waited` "none waits for a raised way" → "a trace waiting by §2.7's crossing table's (G3) among them"; `raised.waited` adds "or one whose strip or fixed-place zone no course keeps clear of a standing trace's gates, towers or fixed places (§2.7's crossing table, *over the band*)". * Under V07 (E-V7-4): §3.13 adds "| F-V-RAISED the palisade meets a raised way with no lawful crossing, or a fixed place with no clear point (§2.7's crossing table, (G3)) | VS3 | the ring re-pulled once with the under-deck strip impassable but at its lawful crossings → the palisade omitted, reported | T-V7-48 |". * Under scope (E-S12): T110-2 adds, on a fixture whose `pierSpacingM` is set by a table edit so that no span's clear width admits the band, each path's (G3) — F-WALL's rung at generation and at a regeneration, `walls.waited` at an epoch, F-V-RAISED at a village, `refuse.raised.meeting` by hand for a stretch and for a fixed place.

issues.cell: The state sweep's C8 (R7-06 (a), E-S0); W3·C8, W7·C8, W8·C8; W3's C1 note ("a held wall standing before every stage met as an unlocked one").
issues.claim: The sweep's C8 is "the raised way locked and, on a second run, pinned — and, in a clause whose event creates or edits the raised way, the wall locked" (adj l. 730–731; E-S0 l. 813–815): never an arch vault the user locked or a declared building seated in one, and never a held wall at a regeneration. Yet W3·C8 asserts "a locked arch vault's chamber under the ring not laid (a `reshaped` entry) · T110-2 (6)·S" (adj l. 495); W7·C8 and W8·C8 (adj l. 499–500) give a locked chamber laid again, locked, after `wallToWay` and after the absorbed record's last dismantle; W3's C1 cell gives a held wall met as an unlocked one at every regeneration stage (S6's aqueduct *over the band* clear of its standing towers, gates and fixed places; S4's priced deck down before it). E-S4 and T-V4-80 (i) run the locked vault only for an epoch circuit, a hand `drawWall` and a hand delete (adj l. 869–874, 1112–1116); E-S1 – E-S2 run a held wall only by hand. A build that keeps a locked chamber under a regenerated ring, re-lays it unlocked after `wallToWay` or the last dismantle, or re-derives a held ring's towers at a regeneration passes every bar — R7-01's "untested edge whose outcome the text defines": MAJOR.
issues.required_change: * R7-06 (a) and E-S0, the sweep's C8: "C8, the raised way locked and, on a second run, pinned — and, in a clause whose event creates or edits the raised way, the wall locked;" → "C8, the raised way locked and, on a second run, pinned; on a third, the `vault` span over the line holding an arch vault the user locked before any wall stood over it (its chamber removed and its lock kept by the lock sentence where the clause's run already stands over it), and on a fourth, a declared placement seated in that vault before the wall event; and, in a clause whose event creates or edits the raised way, the wall locked;". * E-S6 (T110-2 (6)) adds: "; and a CITY whose stage-1 ring was drawn by hand, regenerated (keep) and given New random — the ring held before every stage, (1)'s S6 aqueduct *over the band* with its strip clear of the ring's standing towers and gates and its fixed-place zone of the ring's fixed places, an S4 route priced on a deck across it brought down before it through a standing gate, nothing of the held ring changed but by the lock sentence".

issues.cell: W8·C1 and W8·C11: a raised way created across an absorbed record's standing runs.
issues.claim: W8's C1 and C11 are "—" ("a raised way created after this event meets the wall as the event left it, by W1·C1 or W1·C11", adj l. 478–479). After `absorbWall` "the chain's `wall` role rows are removed ...; its strips re-join the blocks", "its remaining runs keep their `condition`" (V06 l. 717), E-V6-2 adds "its strips, the band with them, re-join the blocks", and plots meet on the old line while the runs stand (V06 l. 1489–1495). *Over the band* keeps supports "off the wall's band by (3)" (adj l. 311–312), and (3)'s obstacle is "an enceinte's band (`Enceinte.band`, or before S10 has built it the band beside the standing trace ...)" (base l. 2537–2539) — none after the absorb. So an aqueduct founded across the old line (V06 §3.19) may stand a pier on a run not yet dismantled — what R7-04 (b) itself calls "no coherent shape" (adj l. 665–667), and against *Where the line crosses*; a road deck may or may not come down before it. Builders differ.
issues.required_change: W8's C1 and C11 cells: "—" → "a raised way created across the absorbed record's standing runs (V06 §3.19's founding, a hand declaration) meets each run not yet `dismantled` as a standing wall — its band as it stood before the absorb an obstacle of (3), *over the band* (an aqueduct) or *down before the wall* (a road deck, that run's line counting as a standing trace), its strip clear of their towers and gates; a `dismantled` run none · T-V6-11·S". Model text (a new (M5)): the support step's (3) "an enceinte's band (`Enceinte.band`, or before S10 has built it the band beside the standing trace, its half-widths by §4.8's rows along the stretch profile)" adds "— an absorbed record's too, over each run not yet `dismantled` (V06 §2.8) —".

issues.cell: (G3) by hand; *over the band*'s "else refused"; *down before the wall* by hand; the bent group's "a moved line stays within (G1)'s reach"; E-S1's refused aqueduct; E-D4.
issues.claim: Item 101 R2 (the owner's): "The tool bends a declaration to the nearest lawful one and says so in one gentle line; it refuses only what item 20 forbids (dossier facts) and what a lock protects, always with the closest alternatives" (docs/AMENDMENTS-2026-09-27e.md item 101). (G3): "by hand its dry run is refused with the nearest lawful declarations (`refuse.raised.meeting`, §7.1; item 101 R2)" (adj l. 295–296); *over the band*: "a declared one bent to the nearest course that can, else refused (G3)" (adj l. 323–324); *down before the wall*: "a course that cannot come down there is refused (`refuse.raised.meeting`, G3)" (adj l. 335–336); the bent group: "a moved line stays within (G1)'s reach ... (G3) holds: by hand `refuse.raised.meeting`" (adj l. 421–423); E-S1: an aqueduct "across a wall where no course keeps its supports off the band ..., refused" (adj l. 823–825), the wall not said to be held. Where nothing a lock protects stands in the way — a hand aqueduct or raised road across a generated, unlocked wall; a hand stretch that could pass round the raised way's end — R2 asks a bend to the nearest lawful declaration (the aqueduct's or road's end brought back before the wall, as `bend.raised.end` brings an end; the stretch carried round the raised way, as `bend.raised.around` takes a way round), not a refusal. (G1) binds a held thing's reshape (adj l. 288–291), not the op's own new line. The guardrail (G3) is the program's (PROGRESS J144, "by hand refused with the nearest lawful alternative, item 101 R2"; J122, vetoable) and cannot narrow the owner's R2.
issues.required_change: * (G3) (adj l. 295–296): "by hand its dry run is refused with the nearest lawful declarations (`refuse.raised.meeting`, §7.1; item 101 R2)" → "by hand its dry run is bent to the nearest lawful declaration that moves and breaks no held thing (item 101 R2: a raised way's end brought back before the wall, `bend.raised.end`; a hand stretch carried round the raised way's end, a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line), and refused (`refuse.raised.meeting`, §7.1, with the nearest lawful declarations) only where every lawful declaration would move or break a held thing". * The bent group (adj l. 421): "a moved line stays within (G1)'s reach" → "(G1) binds the held raised way, never the stretch's own line". * *Over the band* (adj l. 323–324): "else refused (G3)" → "else (G3)"; *down before the wall* (adj l. 335–336): "a course that cannot come down there is refused (`refuse.raised.meeting`, G3)" → "a course that cannot come down there takes (G3)". * E-S1 (adj l. 823–825): "and across a wall where no course keeps its supports off the band within `raisedWays.structure.maxClearSpanM`, refused (`refuse.raised.meeting`), nothing of either built" → "and across a wall drawn by hand where no course keeps its supports off the band within (3)'s bound, refused (`refuse.raised.meeting`), nothing of either built, and across a generated, unlocked wall the same, its end brought back before the wall (`bend.raised.end`)". * E-D4's cause adds, before "(§2.7's crossing table, the lock sentence's (G3))": "where every lawful declaration would move or break a held thing".

issues.cell: The lock sentence's reach (retaining walls and raised ways are similar structures) × E-V6-4 (V06 §3.19 (5)): a founded course meeting a held retaining wall or another held raised way; W1·C1 at E.
issues.claim: The similar structures include "a retaining wall" and "the raised ways" (adj l. 278–280); every change at a meeting "is made whether either side is locked, pinned, declared or neither" (adj l. 282–287); of a retaining wall: "the deck passes over it as over the ground it levels and a support stands on its line built against it" (adj l. 301–303). E-V6-4 keeps "Locked, pinned and declared entities" at the head of the founding's impassable list "to the course's supports, ramps, stairs and feet and to its clearing ((7))", exempting only "a locked, pinned or declared ground way" and "a locked, pinned or declared wall" (adj l. 1173–1181). A drawn retaining wall (T3 `retaining`, held, §7.2) is then impassable to a founded aqueduct's supports and clearing — the course routed round it — while the lock sentence passes the deck over it with a support on its line; a declared viaduct is impassable to a founded aqueduct's clearing where an unheld one is not (only "every other raised way's supports" are). And one list makes a held wall impassable to the clearing in its first clause and passable by the crossing table in its last. A lock alters a meeting of two similar structures (J144: "A lock that refuses or skips a meeting anywhere is a finding").
issues.required_change: E-V6-4: "Locked, pinned and declared entities, dossier-listed buildings," → "Locked, pinned and declared entities — but a wall, a retaining wall and another raised way, which a course meets as unlocked ones (§2.7's crossing table, its lock sentence: a retaining wall passed over, a support on its line built against it) —, dossier-listed buildings,"; and "and meets a locked, pinned or declared wall by §2.7's crossing table as an unlocked one (its lock sentence)" → "and meets a locked, pinned or declared wall, retaining wall or raised way as an unlocked one (§2.7's crossing table, its lock sentence)". Scope's E-S1 third run adds "and across a retaining wall drawn by hand — passed over, a support on its line, nothing of it written (the lock sentence's retaining wall)".

issues.cell: Tests naming a case they do not run: W1·C12, W2·C12; W1·C3 – C6 at V; W13·C9; the sweep's C6; T-V9-13.
issues.claim: W1·C12 and W2·C12 name "T110-2's frame clause" (adj l. 493–494), whose fixture extends the deck across the ring — C12's own event after the row's — not the row's event on an extended deck (the sweep's C12 run does that). W1·C3 – C6 at V and W13·C9 name T-V7-48 (adj l. 493, 505), which runs neither VS3 laid after a fallen span nor a hand `placeGate` at a village. The sweep's C6, "a `vault` span over the line breached with its arch vault" (adj l. 728–729), cannot be made in a clause whose run already stands over the span (no chamber under a wall). T-V9-13 lists the refusal keys that must carry an alternative and omits `refuse.raised.meeting` (V09 l. 4372). The outcomes are each another cell's by construction.
issues.required_change: W1·C12 and W2·C12: "T110-2's frame clause" → "T110-2 (4)·S (its C12 run)"; E-V7-1 adds "; VS3's palisade re-laid after a span over its line fell (row W1·C3 at a village) and a hand `placeGate` inside the strip at the village (W13·C9)"; E-S0's C6 "a `vault` span over the line breached with its arch vault" → "a `vault` span over the line breached (with its arch vault where no wall stood over it before the event)"; a new END under V09 (E-V9-7): T-V9-13's list "`refuse.warp`, `refuse.water`" → "`refuse.warp`, `refuse.water`, `refuse.raised.meeting`".

issues.cell: Readers (blind spots (b), (d)): V09 §4.20.2 (4); V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.aqueductArch` source cell; E-V6-5.
issues.claim: V09 §4.20.2 (4): "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall crosses it on one of its arches, its supports off the band and its course clear of that wall's towers and gates" (V09 l. 3016–3017), and `bend.wall.aqueductArch`'s source cell (V09 l. 2102), keep no fixed places and no held wall; E-V9-6 rewrites only the paragraph's last words. E-V6-5's "nor a fixed place's zone" (adj l. 1184–1185) names a zone the fixed-place sentence gives a raised way, not a fixed place.
issues.required_change: E-V9-6 adds: "its course clear of that wall's towers and gates" → "its course clear of that wall's towers and gates and its fixed-place zone of the wall's fixed places, a held wall as an unlocked one (§2.7's crossing table, its lock and fixed-place sentences)"; and `bend.wall.aqueductArch`'s source cell "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall" → "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, held or not". E-V6-5: "nor a fixed place's zone" → "nor a standing raised way's fixed-place zone at a fixed place".

issues.cell: (G2): E-D7's derivation of a `reshaped` entry; the village path.
issues.claim: E-D7 derives a `reshaped` entry "from the lifecycle event the change writes on the held entity" (adj l. 1048–1049), but a held raised way's chamber removed or laid again writes nothing on the raised way ("nothing of the raised way written"), so the entry the lock sentence promises for "each removal and re-lay of a held raised way's ... chamber" (adj l. 368–369) has no source. (G2) names generation, a regeneration and an epoch (adj l. 293–294), not a village derivation, which (G3) names (adj l. 299). The report is derived, never canonical.
issues.required_change: E-D7: "— derived, as every entry is, from the lifecycle event the change writes on the held entity" → "— derived, as every entry is, from the lifecycle event the change writes on the held entity, or, for a held raised way's chamber, on the chamber (`entity` the raised way, `met` the wall)"; (G2) (adj l. 293): "at generation, at a regeneration and at an epoch" → "at generation, at a regeneration, at an epoch and at a village derivation".

issues.cell: The bent group's counting × *Reported* and the paths note.
issues.claim: The bent group: "Each move is a fate by hand, ... and counted at an epoch (`walls.raisedCrossings`)" (adj l. 420–421). *Reported*: "once per crossing of a trace laid after a raised way with that raised way's deck line" (adj l. 389–391); the paths note: "`W_RAISED_CROSSING` and `walls.raisedCrossings` count only a trace laid after a raised way crossing its deck line ... and a channel stopped" (adj l. 482–483). A part moved to the strip's edge (ii) crosses no deck line. The counter is derived.
issues.required_change: (adj l. 420–421): "and counted at an epoch (`walls.raisedCrossings`)" → "and at an epoch the stretch's crossings of the deck line counted in `walls.raisedCrossings` as *Reported* says (a move is no count)".

issues.cell: R7-04 (d) and the way-and-channel row (c): `wallToWay`'s dry run.
issues.claim: "each `vault` span the old wall stood over read `vault` (no band, strip or run lies there once the op commits ...)" (adj l. 693–694; row (c), adj l. 527) is false where another enceinte's band or strip, or an absorbed record's standing run, still meets the span (a contraction inside the old ring; a later circuit near it); *beneath* then reads it `open`, and V04 lays no chamber.
issues.required_change: R7-04 (d) and row (c): "each `vault` span the old wall stood over read `vault` (no band, strip or run lies there once the op commits" → "each `vault` span the old wall stood over and no other wall's band, strip or standing run meets read `vault` (no band, strip or run of the old wall lies there once the op commits".

issues.cell: Hand paths with no row: a hand `contractWall`, a hand `wearWall`, a hand `neglect`.
issues.claim: §7.1's T3 converts include `contractWall`, `wearWall` and `neglect` (base l. 10588); `contractWall` "traces and builds the new ring inside the old one through S5a's trace step and S7's operator" (base l. 8662). W1's paths are G, V and E (adj l. 493); W5's are "(E; V: V07 §3.4 (8))" (adj l. 497). The outcomes follow W1 (a pulled trace) and W5 (*unchanged meeting*) by construction, but a hand contraction's dry-run line and fates are unstated.
issues.required_change: W1's event cell adds "; a hand `contractWall` (H; its dry run a hand `convert`'s line, each held thing's change the fate *reshaped*, no bend)"; W5's paths "(E; V: V07 §3.4 (8))" → "(E; V: V07 §3.4 (8); H: a hand `convert` `wearWall` or `neglect`)".

issues.cell: *Down before the wall* by hand: the drawn course beyond the trace.
issues.claim: "By hand the course comes down before the trace (§7.1, `bend.raised.wall`), its ground way making its gate there" (adj l. 334–335); §7.1 *Raised ways* says the same (base l. 10484–10486). A stroke from `P1` to `P2` beyond the wall leaves its part past the trace unstated — a second deck rising again, a ground way to `P2`, or dropped.
issues.required_change: (adj l. 335) after "its ground way making its gate there" add "— the stroke's course beyond the trace carried on as that ground way on ground part 0 to its end (a second raised way only by a second declaration) —".

issues.cell: The lock sentence's retaining-wall clause: a support on its line.
issues.claim: "a support stands on its line built against it, its height read at its station ((4))" (adj l. 302–303); (4) reads "the deck's level less `levelledGroundCm` at its station", and a retaining wall's line carries two levelled grounds, so the pier's height, and (4)'s `maxPierM` bound, depend on the side read.
issues.required_change: "its height read at its station ((4))" → "its height read at its station on the low side ((4): the deck's level less the lower `levelledGroundCm` there)".

issues.cell: W4's, W8's and W11's last columns: a held chamber laid again.
issues.claim: W7's last column names "the re-route and the vault a fate (a held vault's *reshaped*)" (adj l. 499); W11's reads "fates in the dry run; no bend" (adj l. 503), and W4's (the last dismantle's re-lay, adj l. 496) and W8's (adj l. 500) name no fate, though the lock sentence shows "each removal and re-lay of a held raised way's or a held arch vault's chamber ... by (G2)" (adj l. 368–369).
issues.required_change: W4's, W8's and W11's last columns add "; a chamber laid again a fate (a held one's *reshaped*)".
